title: I study, you work
summary: Say where people study, work and live, with present-tense verbs for I, you, we and they.
intro: Three useful verbs today: يَدْرُسُ (to study), يَعْمَلُ (to work) and يَسْكُنُ (to live). With نَحْنُ (we) the prefix is نَ: نَدْرُسُ (we study). With أَنْتُمْ (you, to a group) and هُمْ (they) the verb also ends in ـُونَ: هُمْ يَعْمَلُونَ (they work).
objectives: Say where you study, work and live
Ask someone where they work or live
Use present-tense verbs with we, you (to a group) and they
Name places of study and work: جَامِعَة, مَكْتَب, شَرِكَة

realLife.title: A friend from Amman
realLife.story: After class Sami brings his friend Yusuf from Jordan to the café near the school. Yusuf is in Cairo for a few months for his company, and he studies in the evenings too. Daniel wants to know how he does both.

sentences.literal: we study the Arabic in Cairo

mistakes.why: With 'we' the prefix is na-: nadrusu. a- is only for 'I'.

sentences.en: They work in a big office.
sentences.literal: they work in an office big

mistakes.why: With 'they' the verb ends in -ūna: yaʿmalūna.

sentences.en: Do you study at the university? (to a group)

sentences.ar: يُوسُف يَعْمَلُ فِي شَرِكَة، وَيَدْرُسُ فِي الْمَسَاء.
sentences.en: Yusuf works at a company, and he studies in the evening.
sentences.literal: Yusuf works in a company, and he studies in the evening

dialogue.title: Work by day, study by night
dialogue.culture: It is common for a friend from another Arab city to stay with a family for a while, and guests are treated generously. أَهْلًا بِكَ (welcome to you) is said with real warmth, and the guest is often called one of the family.

lines.ar: يَا أَصْدِقَاء، تَذْكُرُونَ يُوسُف؟ هُوَ الْآن فِي الْقَاهِرَة لِلْعَمَل.
lines.en: Friends, do you remember Yusuf? He is in Cairo for work now.

lines.ar: طَبْعًا! أَهْلًا يَا يُوسُف. أَيْنَ تَعْمَلُ هُنَا فِي الْقَاهِرَة؟
lines.en: Of course! Hi, Yusuf. Where do you work here in Cairo?

lines.ar: أَهْلًا بِكَ! أَعْمَلُ فِي مَكْتَبِ شَرِكَة أُرْدُنِّيَّة، قَرِيب مِنَ النِّيل.
lines.en: Welcome to you too! I work in the office of a Jordanian company, near the Nile.
segs: to you, with you (to a man)

lines.ar: وَمَاذَا تَعْمَلُ فِي الشَّرِكَة؟ هَلْ أَنْتَ مُهَنْدِس؟
lines.en: And what do you do at the company? Are you an engineer?
segs: you work, you do (to a man)

lines.ar: لَا، أَنَا مُوَظَّف. أَعْمَلُ مِنَ السَّاعَة التَّاسِعَة إِلَى السَّاعَة الْخَامِسَة.
lines.en: No, I am an office worker. I work from nine o'clock to five o'clock.

lines.ar: وَأَيْنَ تَسْكُنُ؟ هَلْ تَسْكُنُ قَرِيبًا مِنَ الْمَكْتَب؟
lines.en: And where do you live? Do you live near the office?

lines.ar: أَسْكُنُ مَعَ سَامِي وَعَائِلَتِهِ فِي شَارِعِ النِّيل. هُمْ عَائِلَة كَرِيمَة جِدًّا!
lines.en: I live with Sami and his family on Nile Street. They are a very generous family!

lines.ar: وَيُوسُف يَدْرُسُ أَيْضًا! يَدْرُسُ الْإِنْجِلِيزِيَّة فِي الْجَامِعَة فِي الْمَسَاء.
lines.en: And Yusuf studies too! He studies English at the university in the evening.

lines.ar: تَعْمَلُ فِي النَّهَار وَتَدْرُسُ فِي الْمَسَاء؟ هٰذَا صَعْب!
lines.en: You work during the day and study in the evening? That is hard!

lines.ar: نَعَم، قَلِيلًا. وَأَنْتُمْ؟ هَلْ تَدْرُسُونَ فِي الْجَامِعَة أَيْضًا؟
lines.en: Yes, a little. And you? Do you all study at the university too?

lines.ar: لَا، نَحْنُ نَدْرُسُ الْعَرَبِيَّة فِي مَدْرَسَةِ اللُّغَة، كُلَّ يَوْم مِنَ الْأَحَد إِلَى الْخَمِيس.
lines.en: No, we study Arabic at the language school, every day from Sunday to Thursday.

lines.ar: وَنَحْنُ نَعْمَلُ كَثِيرًا أَيْضًا! عِنْدَنَا وَاجِب كُلَّ يَوْم.
lines.en: And we work hard too! We have homework every day.

lines.ar: صَحِيح! وَأَيْنَ تَسْكُنُونَ؟ هَلْ تَسْكُنُونَ قَرِيبًا مِنَ الْمَدْرَسَة؟
lines.en: That's true! And where do you all live? Do you live near the school?

lines.ar: أَنَا أَسْكُنُ فِي بَيْتِ الطَّالِبَات، وَدَانْيَال يَسْكُنُ مَعَ عَائِلَة مِصْرِيَّة.
lines.en: I live in a hostel for women students, and Daniel lives with an Egyptian family.

lines.ar: هَيَّا يَا أَصْدِقَاء، نَشْرَبُ الشَّاي الْآن. يُوسُف يَعْمَلُ غَدًا فِي السَّاعَة التَّاسِعَة!
lines.en: Come on, friends, let's drink our tea now. Yusuf works tomorrow at nine o'clock!

reading.title: Students and workers
reading.ar: سَامِي وَلَيْلَى وَأَنَا طُلَّاب. نَحْنُ نَدْرُسُ الْعَرَبِيَّة فِي الصَّبَاح. يُوسُف مُوَظَّف، وَالْمُوَظَّفُونَ فِي شَرِكَتِهِ يَعْمَلُونَ مِنَ السَّاعَة التَّاسِعَة إِلَى السَّاعَة الْخَامِسَة. بَعْضُهُمْ يَدْرُسُونَ فِي الْجَامِعَة فِي الْمَسَاء. وَأَنْتُمْ؟ هَلْ تَعْمَلُونَ أَوْ تَدْرُسُونَ؟
reading.en: Sami, Layla and I are students. We study Arabic in the morning. Yusuf is an office worker, and the employees at his company work from nine o'clock to five o'clock. Some of them study at the university in the evening. And you? Do you work or study?

quiz.prompt: In the dialogue, where does Yusuf live in Cairo?
Which word means 'they' (for a group of men or a mixed group)?
Which word has the throat sound ʿayn?

completion: Well done! You can say where people study, work and live, and use verbs with we, you and they.
